## Traps — where memory gives a DIFFERENT answer

Read before asserting anything in these areas.

- **R-GLOS-001** — Calling attack rolls or saving throws ability checks merely because they also use an ability modifier.
- **R-GLOS-002** — Using "ability" to mean only the modifier or only the score when the distinction changes arithmetic.
- **R-GLOS-003** — Treating AC as damage reduction.
- **R-GLOS-004** — Treating a spell that forces only a saving throw as a spell attack.
- **R-GLOS-005** — Treating Bloodied as a condition or as exactly half Hit Points only.
- **R-GLOS-006** — Calling cantrips level 1 spells because 1 is the lowest slot level.
- **R-GLOS-007** — Treating Concentration as a spell-only mechanic; other effects can require it too.
- **R-GLOS-008** — Assuming "creature" excludes player characters or includes unattended objects.
- **R-GLOS-009** — Confusing Hit Dice with the dice rolled for weapon damage.
- **R-GLOS-010** — Treating a saving throw as an ability check; both are D20 Tests but are distinct kinds.
- **R-GLOS-011** — Treating a slot as a specific prepared spell rather than a level-bounded casting resource.
- **R-GLOS-012** — Adding Proficiency Bonus to every D20 Test, or adding it more than once without a rule such as Expertise multiplying it.
- **R-ABIL-001** — Using the later general score cap of 20 as the point-buy maximum, or pricing 14 and 15 as one point per increase.
- **R-ABIL-003** — Applying the 2014 species ability score increases, or adding both species and background increases.
- **R-ABIL-004** — Awarding an ASI whenever total character level reaches 4, 8, and so on. Multiclass characters must reach the feature level in a class.
- **R-ABIL-005** — Rounding toward zero for scores below 10. The equivalent calculation rounds down, so 9 gives −1.
- **R-COMBAT-001** — Remembering only the level-3 range, or applying the level-15 range at total character level 15 rather than Fighter level 15.
- **R-COMBAT-002** — Treating every D20 Test as an automatic success on 20 and automatic failure on 1.
- **R-COMBAT-003** — Applying Resistance before a flat reduction, or cancelling Resistance and Vulnerability before other modifiers.
- **R-COMBAT-004** — Doubling only the weapon die, or doubling the flat ability modifier too.
- **R-COMBAT-005** — Adding a flat bonus or penalty instead of selecting one of two d20 rolls.
- **R-COMBAT-006** — Netting sources numerically, such as two Advantages versus one Disadvantage leaving Advantage.
- **R-COMBAT-007** — Adding multiple cover bonuses together, or applying cover to every saving throw rather than Dexterity saves.
- **R-COMBAT-008** — Adding Proficiency Bonus to an attack with a weapon the attacker lacks proficiency with, or using Dexterity for every thrown weapon.
- **R-COMBAT-009** — Adding Proficiency Bonus by default. It applies only if a feature grants proficiency or another relevant modifier.
- **R-COMBAT-010** — Adding Constitution or Proficiency Bonus by default. A Death Save is not tied to an ability score.
- **R-COMBAT-011** — Treating a natural 20 as two successes rather than immediately regaining 1 Hit Point.
- **R-COMBAT-012** — Comparing damage only with the creature's current 0 Hit Points rather than its Hit Point maximum for instant death.
- **R-COMBAT-013** — Adding Unarmored Defense or Mage Armor on top of 10 + Dexterity, or combining two alternative base formulas.
- **R-COMBAT-014** — Treating armor training only as an AC or movement issue, or applying the armor penalties to an untrained Shield instead of merely losing its AC bonus.
- **R-COMBAT-015** — Importing the Monk's no-Shield clause into Barbarian Unarmored Defense.
- **R-COMBAT-016** — Allowing a Shield because Barbarian Unarmored Defense does, or using Constitution instead of Wisdom.
- **R-COMBAT-017** — Automatically granting every weapon's mastery property to anyone proficient with that weapon.
- **R-COMBAT-018** — Adding a positive ability modifier to the second target's damage or cleaving more than once per turn.
- **R-COMBAT-019** — Rolling the weapon die on a miss or adding other flat damage bonuses to Graze damage.
- **R-COMBAT-020** — Treating Nick as an additional extra attack beyond the one granted by the Light property.
- **R-COMBAT-021** — Allowing Push against Huge or Gargantuan creatures, or in any chosen direction.
- **R-COMBAT-022** — Applying Disadvantage to every attack until your next turn rather than only the next attack roll.
- **R-COMBAT-023** — Stacking the same Slow mastery reduction for every hit.
- **R-COMBAT-024** — Using Strength for the DC regardless of the attack ability, or treating Topple as automatic on hit.
- **R-COMBAT-025** — Granting Advantage against any target or on every later attack during the duration.
- **R-MC-001** — 2014 rules rounded DOWN and recall reproduces that. "Paladin dip is slot-dead" is WRONG. This exact error was asserted in a design doc and shipped to three agent lanes before being caught.
- **R-MC-003** — Assuming a 3rd-level slot lets you cast 3rd-level spells. It does not — it upcasts 1st-level spells.
- **R-MC-004** — Assuming one save DC across a multiclass caster. Each class's spells use that class's ability.
- **R-MC-005** — Assuming a dip grants the class's full starting proficiency list. It does not — check `docs/srd/source/multiclass-entry-grants.txt` for the per-class subset before assuming armour training.
- **R-MC-007** — Treating 7 classes as needing 7 separate 13s. It is a SET COVER over this table — Cha 13 + Wis 13 + Dex 13 alone unlocks seven classes (Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Cleric, Druid, Rogue, Fighter).
- **R-MC-008** — This is proven by ABSENCE, so no QUOTE can establish it — an entry here needs a CHECK. The costly form of the error is not "Warlock 1 is bad" (a 1-level dip is cheap and buys Pact Magic plus an invocation) but a MULTI-LEVEL Warlock dip: Warlock 3 spends 3 of 7 character levels for zero shared-slot progression, collapsing a Shape B mutt from caster level 7 (4/3/3/1) to 4 (4/3) and deleting every 3rd- and 4th-level slot.
- **R-MC-009** — The shared slot table lies to the eye. A seven-dip at character level 7 shows slots up to level 3 (or 4 with a 3-level class) — and can still prepare NOTHING above level 1 (or 2). The quoted sentence is COLUMN-INTERLEAVED in the source ("what spells you Paladin, you have ten d10 Hit Dice"), so a contiguous-sentence QUOTE cannot verify it; the CHECK uses short phrases that survive the interleave. Inverse trap (errata E-mistake #6): "a multiclass prepares only 1st-level spells" is true ONLY when every class is level 1 — state the cap per class, never per character.
- **R-REST-001** — Restoring all Channel Divinity uses on a Short Rest, as older phrasing and memory suggest.
- **R-REST-002** — Assigning one use at level 2 from the 2014 Cleric table.
- **R-REST-003** — Treating Rage as Long-Rest-only because that was the 2014 recovery rule.
- **R-REST-004** — Treating any quiet pause as a completed Short Rest or allowing a creature at 0 Hit Points to start one normally.
- **R-REST-005** — Spending all chosen Hit Dice before seeing any rolls, or allowing a low Constitution modifier to make a die restore 0 Hit Points.
- **R-REST-006** — Letting the creature resume the same Short Rest after combat or a leveled spell without restarting the hour.
- **R-REST-007** — Treating 8 hours of any downtime as a Long Rest without the sleep requirement.
- **R-REST-008** — Restoring only half the character's Hit Dice, which was the 2014 rule.
- **R-REST-009** — Discarding all elapsed rest time after any interruption, or granting Short Rest benefits before 1 hour elapsed.
- **R-REST-010** — Applying Warlock Pact Magic recovery to the shared Spellcasting slot pool.
- **R-SPELL-001** — Applying the cantrip's scaling thresholds to the level in the class that granted it. A one-level caster dip still scales at character levels 5, 11, and 17.
- **R-SPELL-002** — Treating possession of a level 3 slot as access to level 3 spells. Spell preparation is determined for each class independently.
- **R-SPELL-003** — Adding one dart total when upcast, or confusing spell level 4 with four darts.
- **R-SPELL-004** — Applying 2014 half-caster rounding down, adding Pact Magic to shared slots, or using the multiclass table directly for a single-class Paladin or Ranger.
- **R-SPELL-005** — Assuming every spell gains damage, targets, or duration from a higher slot.
- **R-SPELL-006** — Waiting until the new spell finishes casting before ending the old Concentration.
- **R-SPELL-007** — Using half damage rounded up, omitting the DC 30 maximum, or treating this as an ability check.
- **R-SPELL-008** — Assuming Unconscious is a separately listed trigger; it breaks Concentration because Unconscious includes Incapacitated.
- **R-SPELL-009** — Forgetting that the Wizard's Ritual Adept feature overrides the general preparation requirement for Ritual spells in the Wizard's spellbook.
- **R-SPELL-010** — Treating the extra 10-minute casting time as permission to choose a higher spell level.
- **R-SPELL-011** — Using the 2014 vocabulary split where Bard, Sorcerer, and Warlock "know" spells while only some classes prepare them. SRD 5.2.1 calls all of these prepared spells and varies replacement cadence.
- **R-SPELL-012** — Counting subclass, species, background, or feat spells against a class's prepared-spell allowance merely because they appear in the same sheet section.
- **R-SPELL-013** — Adding the full ability score, using class level for proficiency, or assuming every multiclass spell uses the same spellcasting ability.
- **R-SPELL-014** — Applying the 2014 Bonus Action spell restriction. SRD 5.2.1 instead limits the number of spell slots expended to cast spells on a turn.
- **R-SPELL-015** — Applying the general prepared-spell requirement without the Wizard feature's specific exception.

1. `grep -i '<keyword>' .ai/kb/INDEX.md` — answers are inline here.
2. `grep -i '^Q:.*<keyword>' .ai/kb/*.md` — topic entries.
3. Not here? Go to the SOURCE, not to memory. Then ADD the entry.
